contents.entry: Purpose: why a detector outside the host
The probe: where it runs, what it checks, how often
Alerting: its own topic and token, within 3 minutes, a recovery message
Journal: the capped outage journal on the Pi and the host-side emergency path
Availability: the Pi is not confirmed; proof not-run

pointers.shared: The ntfy server, its access model and the phone's subscription; the probe uses its own topic and token on it
The stable page service answers GET /livez without the store and without a key
The tailnet front door the probe reaches the stable page through
The service unit that imports the outage journal on recovery

purpose.s: What broke (review F15, 2026-10-15): every path by which the owner learned of an outage ran on the host and wrote to the store.

A card is a store commit (N-28), a push is a store subscription (N-31, N-52), and the dead man's switch of N-06 is a timer on the same host, so a store that cannot open or a host that is off produced no card, no push and no record.
On the 9.5 hour outage the review measured, nothing outside the host noticed.

The rule here: one probe that is not on the host and does not read or write the store detects the outage, tells the phone within 3 minutes on a channel of its own, says when it is over, and hands its journal to the store once the store is back.

Rejected: a second probe inside WSL (dies with the host); a systemd watchdog (restarts, never tells anyone when the host itself is down); a cloud uptime service (the page is tailnet-only and a third party would need a door into it).
Cost: one small process on one Raspberry Pi, one ntfy topic, one token, and a /livez route on the stable page.

probe.s: Where: coq-probe, a static Go binary (cmd/coq-probe, planned) on one Raspberry Pi of the owner's cluster (${SITE_PI_LAN_ADDR}), run as a systemd system unit coq-probe.service with Restart=always, as its own unprivileged user, joined to the tailnet so it reaches the host the way the owner's phone does.
Dependencies: none on the store, the host, the cluster API or Jenkins; its config file and its journal live on the Pi; its clock is the Pi's NTP clock; everything it times is UTC.
probe.check: GET http://${SITE_TAILNET_HOST}:44900/livez through the front door (N-34); the stable page service answers it from memory with {up, store, page_state, at} and no key, and answers it while the store is down (nodes/N-32/spec.xml#web-security names the route).
GET http://${SITE_TAILNET_HOST}:44900/ and expect the page shell (200, the login page when no cookie); a 200 with store down still counts as page up.
probe.rule: One check pass is both checks, every 30 s, 5 s timeout each, no retry inside a pass: the next pass is the retry.

States, a pure function of the last passes: up; host-down when both checks fail 4 passes in a row; store-down when /livez answers with store down 4 passes in a row; page-down when /livez fails and the stable page fails while the front door answers TCP.
4 failed passes at 30 s is 2 minutes, plus one 5 s timeout and the send bound below, so the alert leaves within 3 minutes of the first failed pass.

wait.fallback: count the pass as failed; the next pass in 30 s is the retry

alerting.s: Channel: the probe publishes to the ntfy server of nodes/N-52/spec.xml#push-delivery on a topic of its own (the probe topic) with a publish token of its own, scoped write-only to that topic; it never uses the bridge's token or topic, so a bridge defect or a revoked bridge token never silences the probe.
The owner's phone subscribes to the probe topic with the read token of #push-delivery; the same instant delivery path applies (upstream poll through ntfy.sh, body fetched over the tailnet).

Messages: one alert per outage at entry into host-down, store-down or page-down (priority urgent, title "coq host down since HH:MMZ" or the state's own words, body the failed check and the outage id); one reminder every 60 min while the outage lasts; one recovery message after 2 passing passes in a row ("coq back at HH:MMZ, down N min"), priority default.

Bound: the send is 3 attempts at 5, 15, 30 s; a send that still fails is written to the journal as alert_failed and retried at the next pass, so a recovery or an alert is never lost while the ntfy server is reachable at all.
No body ever carries a key, a record id or a ticket title: only the state, the times and the outage id.

wait.fallback: journal alert_failed and retry at the next 30 s pass

alerting.risk: A cluster ntfy outage at the same moment as a host outage is not alerted; the probe journals it and the import shows it later. Recorded, not closed: a second channel would be a third party with the owner's data.

journal.s: Probe side: the probe appends one JSON line per state change and per alert send to its journal on the Pi (/var/lib/coq-probe/outages.jsonl), capped at 10000 lines and 16 MiB by rotating the oldest file away (one rotation kept); each line carries outage_id, state, started_at, ended_at, passes_failed, last_error, alerts_sent, alert_failed.

Import: on recovery the host's service (N-06) reads the journal from the probe's read-only GET /journal?since=<outage_id> over the tailnet and commits one host.outage record per closed outage with operation key N-06/host.outage/<outage_id>/r1, so a repeated import is a replay and an outage is recorded once (shared/contracts.xml#operation-keys).

Host side, for the store that is up but cannot take a write: N-01 keeps store.reserve_mib (default 256 MiB, state-store.xml#config-keys) as a pre-allocated file STATE/run/store.reserve that it deletes, once, when free space falls under the floor, so the commits that report the fault (store.full, the alert, the card) have room; the reserve is re-created only after free space is back above floor plus reserve.

When a commit still fails, the deciding node appends the record it could not commit to STATE/run/emergency.jsonl (owner coq-svc, mode 0600, capped at 4 MiB, oldest dropped and counted), and N-06 replays it into the store on recovery with operation key N-06/emergency.replay/<sha256 of the line>/r1; the replay is idempotent and the file is truncated only after every line committed.

Cleanup: the Pi journal by the probe's own rotation; STATE/run/emergency.jsonl by the replay; STATE/run/store.reserve is never a cleanup target (it is the reserve). The nodes that own these paths (N-01, N-06) register them with N-45.

wait.fallback: leave the journal on the Pi and retry on the next N-06 daily tick; a gap is visible as a probe outage with no host.outage record

availability.s: The owner has not confirmed that a Raspberry Pi of the cluster is free to run the probe; the Pi, its tailnet join and the probe topic are assumptions of this volume, not facts.
Until the owner confirms, the probe is not deployed and F15 stays open as a recorded risk: a host or store outage is seen only when the owner opens the page.
availability.proof: Go-live proof: stop coq.service on the host; the phone, locked, receives the store-down or host-down alert within 3 minutes; start it; the recovery message arrives; host.outage for that outage is in the store after the next import. Not run.

Store-down proof: make the store refuse writes on a test state root; /livez reports store down; the probe alerts within 3 minutes; STATE/run/emergency.jsonl holds the refused records and the replay commits each once. Not run.

many-agents.readers: Every node that names an outage the owner must hear of while the store is down cites #alerting; failure-cases.xml cites this volume for the store and host outage cases.
many-agents.writers: One probe per CANON: a second coq-probe on the Pi is refused by its pid lock (/run/coq-probe.lock) and exits 3; a second Pi running it would double every alert, so the deploy manifest names exactly one host.
many-agents.collision: The probe's alert and a card from the recovered store about the same outage: the host.outage import names the outage_id, the card builder's dedupe keys on it, and the owner sees one card after the fact at most.
Two imports of one journal (two N-06 instances during an upgrade): the operation key replays; one host.outage per outage.
